messages.subject: Re: Merge with SPLUS 6 ver2
messages.body_plain:
Can anyone explain why this is happening?

Using SPLUS6 ver2 for Windows:

I type in the following to merge two dataframes according to subject ID and
visit date:
TAF.ALL<-merge(TAF,TAF.AMI, by=c("ID", "DATE"), all.x=T)  # TAF is a
9069x64 df and TAF.AMI is 112x8

SPLUS 6 returns the following:
Problem in paste (x.by.x, as.vector(x[,by.x[i]]), sep="\001"): Unable to
obtain requested dynamic memory. Use traceback () to see stack.

When I use SPLUS2000 for windows the merge works quickly and correctly!

Why is SPLUS 6 unable to process this simple command when SPLUS 2000 can?
Good thing I kept SPLUS2000 installed on my PC!

Thanks in advance.
LaRee

this in the lowest memory possible, I've been able to achieve the results
but it's too complicated and burns up all my memory.  Any ideas to keep
the memory consumption down?

That may depend on the version of S-PLUS, BTW, so it's always helpful to
tell us.

A data frame is basically a list.  At least under S-PLUS 6, my strategy
would be to prepare a list a column at a time, add the right attributes
and the OldClass "data.frame" (see the end of read.table).

In your example

rn <- LETTERS[1:7]
a1 <- 1:5; names(a1) <- rn[-c(2, 5)]
a2 <- c(3,3,2,2); names(a2) <- rn[4:7]
a3 <- c(3,4,4,4,32); names(a3) <- rn[-(2:3)]

res <- vector("list",3)
names(res) <- c("a1", "a2", "a3")
res$a1 <- a1[match(rn, names(a1))]
res$a2 <- a2[match(rn, names(a2))]
res$a3 <- a3[match(rn, names(a3))]
oldClass(res) <- "data.frame"
row.names(res) <- rn

messages.body_plain:
I'm sure this will have been discussed before, but is everyone finding 
S-Plus 6 for Windows particularly buggy?

I've only recently started to spend any time with it and I am finding it 
very erratic. Particularly interesting is that some actions don't work 
properly through the command line, but do work using the GUI. One file can 
be brought into S-plus using the import menu, or into R using read.table, 
but it doesn't import properly into S-Plus 6 using read.table.

Another file will properly draw a histogram using hist in R, or the menu 
in S-Plus 6, but won't draw it properly using hist in SPlus 6. it draws as 
two bars and I cannot get it to do anything other than two bars.

Another example is typing A;B;C which only prints out the value for C.

I also have a range of other problems which I am now keeping a record of, 
but I wondered if everyone is having problems at this very basic level of 
use.

Many thanks,
Graham S

messages.subject: Re: S-Plus 6 buggy ?
messages.body_plain:
> I'm sure this will have been discussed before, but is 
> everyone finding S-Plus 6 for Windows particularly buggy?

Well, S-PLUS does have some bugs, and the most serious ones are listed
on our website (www.insightful.com/support).  But judging from the
volume of support calls compared to previous releases,  I wouldn't
classify S-PLUS 6 as "particularly buggy".  Be sure you have the latest
service release (select Update S-PLUS in the Help menu).

> I've only recently started to spend any time with it and I am 
> finding it very erratic.

Did you report this problem to your local support representative?  There
is a known bug caused by certain printer drivers on Windows 95/98/ME
which can cause erratic behaviour, and the support team provides a
workaround to the problem.  A complete fix will be in S-PLUS 6.1.

I've said it before, but it bears repeating: if you have a problem with
S-PLUS, please do let us know about it by contacting your local support
rep. They can help with the problem at hand, and flag issues to be
resolved in subsequent releases. The problem with "hist" you mention
will take a little investigation with actual data, and the A;B;C
behaviour is by design (use print(A);print(B);print(C) if you really
want output from clauses of compound expressions).  A difference between
R and S-PLUS is not necessarily a bug in S-PLUS -- R is not (and isn't
intended to be) a perfect copy of S-PLUS.

BTW, information on how to contact your local Insightful rep is at:
http://www.insightful.com/contactus/support.asp

# David

messages.body_plain:
Niels Leuthold posted a summary of responses to his query on
"running all models with 3 or less variables",
mentioning the combinations() function of uncertain origin.

combinations() is from the forthcoming Insightful Resampling library,
which contains a fair number of other functions of very general
interest.  In addition to great new bootstrap and other resampling
capabilities, of course -- in particular, bootstrap tilting
confidence intervals offer a 17-1 or 37-1 reduction in the basic
computation requirements, compared to bootstrap percentile or BCa
intervals, respectively.

The library is currently in its last alpha test, with
wider beta testing to start soon.  If you are interested in
testing, or just want to know what is there, see
        http://www.insightful.com/Hesterberg/bootstrap

messages.subject: nlme error messages
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to fit an aymptotic regression with offset model (SSasympOff)

Response is lizard length, explanatory is date. Eventually I'd like to look 
for Sex and Site effects on the rate and asymptote parameters.

274 lizards, caught and measured at varying nos of dates (1 to 27) at 
erratic intervals

Basing my approach on Pinheiro and Bates p297 where they have similarly

variable nos of obsns per experimental unit and problems reaching 
convergence, my code is

new2.nlme <- nlme(SVL ~ SSasympOff(date2, Asym, int, rate),
fixed = Asym + int + rate ~ 1,
random = pdDiag(Asym + int + rate ~ 1),
data = svl12, start = c(62, -225, -6),
control = list(pnlsTol = 1e-006, maxIter = 100))

I can't get the algorithm to converge.

I've tried a large range of starting values (based on nls and subsequent 
nlme fits to the lizards with 3 or more dates).  (Note - I can fit my 
models to these lizards but now want to include the lizards with 1 or 2 
observations)

With some choices of starting values, I get

Problem in nlme.formula(SVL ~ SSasympOff(date2, Asym, i..: Step halving 
factor reduced below minimum in PNLS step

I've reduced pnlsTol already to 1e-6, and further reduction has not helped

(does anyone know the theoretical minimum, by the way?)

With other starting values I get
Problem in solve.qr(a): apparently singular matrix

With others I get

Problem in .Fortran(if(!cmplx) "chol" else "zchol",: subroutine chol: 1 Inf 
value(s) in argument 1

A colleague here also suggested increasing the tolerance to try to get 
convergence but that doesn't help either

Please could you send help by explaining more about what these messages 
mean and/or giving me suggestions for other things to try (and explanations 
if time allows)? I'll summarise answers for the list ...

Thanks

-------------------------------------------------------------------

Head, Statistical Consulting Unit

John Dedman Mathematical Sciences Building, Room G10
Australian National University

messages.subject: Re: Vectorizing 'for' loop?
messages.body_plain:
Calvin,
  See below:

> 
>   count <- count.rows(myFrame)
>   for(i in 1:count) {
>         if(myFrame$v1[i] >= 0.0 && myFrame$v2[i] >= 0.0 && myFrame$v2[i] <
> 60.0) { myFrame$v11[i] <- "NE1" }
>         else if(myFrame$v1[i] >= 0.0 && myFrame$v2[i] >= 60.0 &&
> myFrame$v2[i] < 120.0) { myFrame$v11[i] <- "NE2" }
>         else if(myFrame$v1[i] >= 0.0 && myFrame$v2[i] >= 120.0) {
> myFrame$v11[i] <- "NE3" }
>   }
>   myFrame$v11 <- factor(myFrame$v11, levels=c("NE1", "NE2", "NE3"))

Can v1<0 || v2<0 ever be true? Not that it really matters. I would
suggest something along the following:

myFrame2 <- data.frame(v1=rnorm(1000),v2=rnorm(1000,0,250))
start <- proc.time()[2]
myFrame2$v11a <- factor(cut(x=myFrame2$v1,
                           
breaks=c(floor(min(myFrame2$v1)),0,ceiling(max(myFrame2$v1)))),
                        labels=c("v1<0","v1>0"))
myFrame2$v11b <- factor(cut(x=myFrame2$v2,
                           
breaks=c(floor(min(myFrame2$v2)),0,60,120,ceiling(max(myFrame2$v2)))),
                        labels=c("v2<0","0<v2<60","60<v2<120","v2>120"))
template <- data.frame(v11a=rep(c("v1<0","v1>0"),each=4),
                      
v11b=rep(c("v2<0","0<v2<60","60<v2<120","v2>120"),times=2),
                      
v11=c("NA","NA","NA","NA","NA","NE1","NE2","NE3"))
myFrame2 <- merge(template,myFrame2,all.y=T)
cat("\nCPU TIME =",proc.time()[2]-start,"\n\n")

I used cut to create the categories. Note that the template I created
has NAs which correspond to v1<0 || v2<0. Also note that the breaks I
defined in the cut cannot have values equal to elements in the vector
being cut (e.g. 60 cannot be an element v2). If 60 can be an element of
v2, you will have to adjust the break points to avoid this. Otherwise
v11b will contain NAs. You should also be able to generalise this
approach to arbitrary break points.

CPU TIME:
YOUR METHOD = 0.05
MY METHOD = 0.02

on Splus6.1/Win2000Pro

Sundar

--

### ORIGINAL POST ###
Could someone give me an example of what this statement means?

``Objects must be assigned to the working data directory before they can
be modified by replacement functions. Earlier versions of S-PLUS
automatically assigned the modified object to the working data.''

but I'm unable to verify its implication.

>

> [1] "data"

>

>

messages.subject: Summary: Vectorizing 'for' loop?
messages.body_plain:
Within 16 hours of posting the question, I got 15 responses from the
following individuals: Brad J. Biggerstaff, Nick Ellis, Chuck Taylor, Samuel
Buttrey, S.D. Byers, James Holtman, Jingshan Zhang, Petr Pikal, Bert Gunter,
Andy Liaw, Jean V. Adams, Leonid Gibiansky, David L. Lorenz, Malcolm Hawkes,
and Sundar Dorai-Raj. Thanks to each and everyone of you.

The responses fell neatly into one of three categories: (a) subscripting the
data frame - 6, (b) using "ifelse" - 6, and (c) using "cut" - 4. Since the
solutions in each category were similar, I chose to include only one from
each. Since the first method seemed to be the simplest to me, I decided to
use it in my application.

(a) subscripting the data frame by Brad J. Biggerstaff
myFrame$v11 <- rep("",nrow(myFrame)) # just to set up an empty character
vector
myFrame[myFrame$v1 >= 0 & myFrame$v2 >= 0 & myFrame$v2 < 60,"v11"] <- "NE1"
myFrame[myFrame$v1 >= 0 & myFrame$v2 >= 60 & myFrame$v2 < 120,"v11"] <-
"NE2"
myFrame[myFrame$v1 >= 0 & myFrame$v2 >= 120,"v11"] <- "NE3"
myFrame$v11 <- factor(myFrame$v11)

(b) using "ifelse" by David L. Lorenz
myFrame$v11 <- ifelse(myFrame$v1 >= 0.0 & myFrame$v2 >= 0.0 & myFrame$v2[i]
< 60.0, "NE1",
               ifelse(myFrame$v1 >= 0.0 & myFrame$v2 >= 60.0 & myFrame$v2 <
120.0, "NE2",
               ifelse(myFrame$v1 >= 0.0 & myFrame$v2 >= 120.0, "NE3", NA)))

(c) using "cut" by Jean V. Adams
myFrame$v11 <- cut(myFrame$v2, breaks=c(0, 60, 120, max(myFrame$v2)+1),
     labels=c("NE1", "NE2", "NE3"), factor.result=T, left.include=T)

The more I use S-PLUS, the more I am appreciating its versatility. Needless
to say, this group is very helpful.

messages.subject: Re: Memory Usage During Script Execution
messages.body_plain:
The script window in S-PLUS for Windows works by collecting the selected
text into a string, and passing it to the function "source".  It
actually calls the function script.run to do this, if you'd like to see
the code.

As a result, some (but not all) intermediate calculations are retained
in memory, so that if an error occurs during script execution, the
working database can be restored to the state before the script was run
(this is a property of the "source" function).

If you want to make each expression evaluate and commit immediately
(which often uses less memory) you can either:

1. cut and paste into the Commands window

2. Call Splus from the command line on your script file, e.g.
  
    Splus < myscript.ssc > outfile.txt
 or
    Sqpe < myscript.ssc > outfile.txt

[Sqpe uses slightly less memory, but won't work if your script relies on
any of the Windows GUI features; notably the function guiCreate.]

3. Wrap the code into a function call (objects created in evaluation
frames outside of the working databases don't need to be rolled back if
an error occurs)

I wanted to make it an option in S-PLUS 6.1 so that the script window
could optionally commit each statement as it's evaluated, like the
command window does, but for architectural reasons that proved tricky to
do.  I'll revisit the issue for 6.2.

# David Smith

messages.body_plain:
Folks:
I have a question pertaining to cleaning raw data from a variety of
sources.
Instead of writing many small functions to alter data (e.g. take one
source's "999s" out and replace them with NAs, or delete certain rows), I
want to write a generic routine.

The input to this would be dataframe like this:
Flags Rules Actions
0     "<="  NA
999   "="   NA
-3    "="   removeRow
Any   my.func     0

and vectors or dataframes of raw data:
 x <- c( 235.6, 232.5, 368.2, 335.1, 209.9, 193.2,   NA, 357.8,  999,   -9,
-20, 468.1, 381.3, 393.1,   NA, 400.7)

I would like to combine the flags, rules and actions vectors so that the
first rule is combined with the first flag and then the first action is
applied if true, e.g.
"look in vector x for values that are <=0; if you find it, set it to NA"
"look in vector x for values that are =999; if you find it, set it to NA"
"look in vector x for values that are =-3; if you find it remove the row"
"apply myfunc to all elements of the vector; set those elements for which
myfunc is TRUE  to 0"

I have a couple of conceptual problems with this:
1) I want to avoid the for loops  since the input data can be LONG
2) I need to extract the elements of rules (e.g. "<=" or myFunc)  and use
as operators...
Any ideas?  Has anyone done something like this before?  If this is not the
right way to go about it, any other approaches?

Thanks,
Yannis Tzamouranis

messages.body_plain:
Hi Christl

 

I've searched the s-news pages for any help on the
problem with the multi-dimensional scaling and I can't find anything. I
was thinking of sending the following to s-news, but thought I'd send it
to you first, in case you think it doesn't make sense, etc.

 

Cheers,

 

James.

 

 

Subject: biases when using multiple variable types in
"daisy"

 

I'm currently using the function "daisy"
to create a dissimilarity matrix and I'm concerned by the way it deals
with ordinal variables. In particular, I have several ordinal variables with
differing numbers of categories; since "daisy" transforms the
ordinal numbers so that they lie in [0,1], this means that the dissimilarity
between two items is higher if they differ on a binary variable, than if they
differ quite substantially in an ordinal variable with say eight categories.
Hence, when "daisy" is used in combination with "cmdscale",
is the method unduly influenced by those variables with a smaller number of
categories and if so, is there a sensible way around this?

 

Thanks,

 

James Lewis.

messages.subject_clean: Constraining y-intercept for a nonlin fit
messages.body_plain:
I have a question regarding specifying CONSTRAINTS (on the y-intercept) with a 
nonlinear model.

What I am trying to do is fit a growth equation to length (mm) at age (years) 
data.

The growth equation is as follows: FLEN = Linf*(1-exp(-k*(AGE-t0))

The input variables are FLEN (dependent) and AGE.

The parameters are Linf, k and t0.

Linf is the asymptote, k is the rate of approach and t0 is the age at which the 
dependent variable (FLEN) is 0.

When fitting this equation I am assuming t0 to be 0 so that the curve always 
goes through the origin. The equation simply becomes: FLEN = Linf*(1-exp(-
k*AGE))

Assuming t0=0 is not always 'biologically' reasonable so what I want to do is 
constrain the y-intercept to a range of reasonable values (let's say between 
10mm-20mm)

How do I do this?

I am sending you a data set which may help you with this (The first colum is 
FLEN and the second colum is AGE. I've included the titles in the file. The 
file is text format (tab delimited)).

I would really appreciate any help on this.

Karine Beauchamp =)

S-PLUS.txt

messages.subject: Summary: group/merge or is.element?
messages.body_plain:
Dear S group;

A while back I posted a question:

a1_data.frame(1:5,row.names=c("A","C","D","E","G"))             
a2_data.frame(c(2,3,3,2,2),row.names=c("B","D","E","F","G"))
a3_data.frame(c(3,4,4,4,32),row.names=c("A","D","E","F","G"))

and I wanted to combine them by grouping by row.names, leaving NA's where
the holes were.
This is a situation where large numbers of columns would cause memory issues
and I wanted the most efficient method possible.

Group and merge were the most straightforward solutions and most popular
answer. Match and is.element save time and memory (18 to 20% for time and
40% of available RAM when using datasets of 360,000x20 over group/merge).
This problem was most quickly solved by calculating outside a function using
match/is.element and combining into a data.frame.  oldClass is a very useful
class to remember.

Thanks to Sundar, Brian Ripley, Trevor Marshall, Jean Adams, Bert Gunter and
Hugh Jones.

#######################################

This should work:

a1 <- data.frame(group=LETTERS[c(1,3,4,5,7)],value1=1:5)
a2 <- data.frame(group=LETTERS[c(2,4:7)],value2=c(2,3,3,2,2))
a3 <- data.frame(group=LETTERS[c(1,4:7)],value3=c(3,4,4,4,32))

a <- merge(a1,a2,by="group",all=T)
merge(a,a3,by="group",all=T)

Sundar Dorai-Raj
#########################################

rn <- LETTERS[1:7]
a1 <- 1:5; names(a1) <- rn[-c(2, 5)]
a2 <- c(3,3,2,2); names(a2) <- rn[4:7]
a3 <- c(3,4,4,4,32); names(a3) <- rn[-(2:3)]

res <- vector("list",3)
names(res) <- c("a1", "a2", "a3")
res$a1 <- a1[match(rn, names(a1))]
res$a2 <- a2[match(rn, names(a2))]
res$a3 <- a3[match(rn, names(a3))]
oldClass(res) <- "data.frame"
row.names(res) <- rn

Brian Ripley
#############################################

sub <- merge(a1,a2,all.x=Tally=T)
res <- merge(sub,a3, all.x=T,all.y=T) 

Trevor Marshall
#########################################

One approach is to make use of the match() function.
I'm not sure how memory efficient it will be on your data.

a <- data.frame(a=rep(NA, 7), row.names=c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F","G"))
a1 <- data.frame(a1=1:5, row.names=c("A", "C", "D", "E", "G"))
a2 <- data.frame(a2=c(2, 3, 3, 2, 2), row.names=c("B", "D", "E", "F", "G"))
a3 <- data.frame(a3=c(3, 4, 4, 4, 32), row.names=c("A", "D", "E", "F","G"))

a[, 1] <- a1[match(dimnames(a)[[1]], dimnames(a1)[[1]]), ]
a[, 2] <- a2[match(dimnames(a)[[1]], dimnames(a2)[[1]]), ]
a[, 3] <- a3[match(dimnames(a)[[1]], dimnames(a3)[[1]]), ]

Jean Adams
######################################################
quite similar to BDR's solution:

foo<-list(a1,a2,a3)
nm<-unique(names(unlist(foo))) ## id's for all the rows needed
out<-sapply(foo,function(x){z<-rep(NA,length(nm))
z[is.element(nm,names(x))]
<-x;z})

Notes:
1) is.element is a simple wrapper for match() -- so this is the similar
to Ripley's solution.

2)out will be a matrix. Convert as needed.

3) This may not work when called within a function because the scoping rules
may not allow nm to be found. Just pass nm as an argument into sapply() then
(e.g., by adding ,nm=nm  to the sapply() functuon call).

4) z could have been computed outside the sapply() call and passed in, of
course. This might save a hair of time.

Let us know which of these worked best for you. Yours was an interesting
question, as evidenced by BDR's reply.

Bert Gunter
########################################
a1 <- data.frame(x=c("A", "C", "D","E","G"), y=1:5)
a2 <- data.frame(x=c("B", "D", "E","F","G"), y=c(2,3,3,2,2))
a3 <- data.frame(x=c("A", "D", "E","F","G"), y=c(3,4,4,4,32))
z <- merge(a1,a2, by=1, all.x=T, all.y=T)
merge(z,a3, by=1, all.x=T, all.y=T)
Hugh Jones

The 2002 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (IEEE ICDM '02)
provides a leading international forum for the sharing of original
research results and practical development experiences among
researchers and application developers from different data mining
related areas such as machine learning, automated scientific
discovery, statistics, pattern recognition, knowledge acquisition,
soft computing, databases and data warehousing, data visualization,
and knowledge-based systems.  The conference seeks solutions to
challenging problems facing the development of data mining systems,
and shapes future directions of research by promoting high quality,
novel and daring research findings.  As an important part of the
conference, the workshops program will focus on new research
challenges and initiatives.

Topics of Interest
==================

Topics related to the design, analysis and implementation of data
mining theory, systems and applications are of interest.  These
include, but are not limited to the following areas:

  - Foundations and principles of data mining 
  - Data mining algorithms and methods in traditional areas (such as
    classification, clustering, probabilistic modeling, and
    association analysis), and in new areas
  - Data and knowledge representation for data mining 
  - Modeling of structured, textual, temporal, spatial, multimedia and
    Web data to support data mining
  - Complexity, efficiency, and scalability issues in data mining
  - Data pre-processing, data reduction, feature selection and feature
    transformation
  - Statistics and probability in large-scale data mining
  - Soft computing (including neural networks, fuzzy logic,
    evolutionary computation, and rough sets) and uncertainty
    management for data mining
  - Integration of data warehousing, OLAP and data mining 
  - Man-machine interaction in data mining and visual data mining 
  - Artificial intelligence contributions to data mining 
  - High performance and distributed data mining 
  - Machine learning, pattern recognition and automated scientific
    discovery
  - Quality assessment and interestingness metrics of data mining
    results
  - Process centric data mining and models of data mining process 
  - Security and social impact of data mining 
  - Emerging data mining applications, such as electronic commerce,
    bioinformatics, Web intelligence, and intelligent learning database 
    systems

Conference Publications and ICDM Best Paper Awards
==================================================

High quality papers in all data mining areas are solicited.  Papers
exploring new directions will receive a careful and supportive review.

There are two different types of paper submission for IEEE ICDM '02:
   (1) main track submissions and 
   (2) industry track submissions.

For the main track submission, all submitted papers should be limited
to a maximum of 6,000 words (approximately 20 A4 pages), and will be
reviewed by the Program Committee on the basis of technical quality,
relevance to data mining, originality, significance, and
clarity. Accepted papers will be published in the conference
proceedings by the IEEE Computer Society Press. All main track paper
submissions will be handled electronically. Please use the Submission
Form (for main track) at the ICDM '02 webpage: 
http://kis.maebashi-it.ac.jp/icdm02

Does anyone have code to share for simulating repeated measurement data using 
one or more correlation structures along with random intercepts or random 
intercepts and random slopes for subjects?

Frank

messages.subject: SUMMARY: Pairwise combination -REVISED-
messages.body_plain:
Dear 
All,

I wanna thank David Lorenz, Sundar Dorai-Raj & Anne York for 
their prompt and helpful suggestions from which I solved my problem. Below are 
the suggestions:

RAY 
HARAF:

M<-rbind(c(0,0,1,2),c(1,1,3,0),c(2,0,0,3))
m <- 
matrix(0,nrow(M),nrow(M))
ij.row <- 
rbind(col(m)[lower.tri(m)],row(m)[lower.tri(m)]) #here credit goes to 
Nick Ellis
adjrow <- lapply(seq(1,choose(nrow(M),2,T),2), 
function(i){
rbind(M[ij.row,][c(i,i+1),])})

SUNDAR DORAI-RAJ 
1:

Ray,
  This should work:
mat <- 
rbind(c(0,0,1,2),c(1,1,3,0),c(2,0,0,3),c(1,4,2,4))
rows <- 
expand.grid(r1=1:nrow(mat),r2=1:nrow(mat))
rows <- 
rows[rows$r1<rows$r2,]
lapply(split(rows,1:nrow(rows)),
      
function(x,M) {
        x <- 
unlist(x)
        
rbind(M[x[1],],M[x[2],])
      
},M=mat)

Tested on SPLUS6/Win2000Pro.

Sundar

SUNDAR 
DORAI-RAJ 2:

Or better yet:
mat <- 
rbind(c(0,0,1,2),c(1,1,3,0),c(2,0,0,3),c(1,4,2,4))
rows <- 
expand.grid(r1=1:nrow(mat),r2=1:nrow(mat))
rows <- 
rows[rows$r1<rows$r2,]
lapply(split(rows,1:nrow(rows)),function(x,M) 
M[unlist(x),],M=mat)

Sundar

ANNE YORK: (Refers to erroneous 
version of the problem as posted earlier)

An easier way might be to apply 
the expand.grid function to each pair of vectors. Your example doesn't do 
exactly what you said because you don't have the combinations from row 2 and row 
3. Here's one way to do this:
Here is your matrix:
> 
mat
     [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
[1,]    
0    0    1    
2
[2,]    1    1    
3    0
[3,]    2    
0    0    3
[3,]    
2    0    0    3

Define an 
array of all the combination you want-- this can be generalized to more than 3 
arrays.

> foo <-expand.grid(1:2,2:3)
> foo
  Var1 
Var2
1    1    2
2    
2    2
3    1    
3
4    2    3

define a new function to 
concatanate the rows:

> 
cmat_function(rows){apply(unlist(mat[rows,]),1,c)}

for example, 
> 
cmat(1:2)
     [,1] [,2]
[1,]    
0    1
[2,]    0    
1
[3,]    1    3
[4,]    
2    0

Use it more generally. Note that the form of the 
output is not exactly what you want, but you can get around that. 
> 
apply(foo,2,cmat)
      Var1 
Var2
 [1,]    0    
1
 [2,]    0    
1
 [3,]    1    
3
 [4,]    2    
0
 [5,]    1    
1
 [6,]    1    
1
 [7,]    3    
3
 [8,]    0    
0
 [9,]    0    
2
[10,]    0    0
[11,]    
1    0
[12,]    2    
3
[13,]    1    2
[14,]    
1    0
[15,]    3    
0
[16,]    0    3
 Hope this 
helps.
Anne

DAVID LORENZ:

Ray,
  I don't have a 
direct solution, but I do have a suggestion for an approach.  I think that 
you need to first create an index of all combinations that you want.  in 
this case it would look like:
    [,1] [,2]
[1,]  
1    2
[2,]  1    3
[3,]  
2    3
  Then all you need to do is extract the rows that 
you want.  I don't have any experience creating a matrix like the one that 
I suggest, but others may.
Dave

Cheers,
Ray 
Haraf.

messages.subject: Composing a Data QC Filter based on vectors of rules and actions
messages.subject_clean: Composing a Data QC Filter based on vectors of rules and actions
messages.body_plain:
The answer to this question came from SPLUS (through Susan Rasch)
The following function will do everything I asked for (applies all filters,
as stated in the Flags, Rules & Actions vectors) sequentially:

"filter.seq"<-
function(x, rules, Actions, flags)
{

   for(i in seq(along = rules)) {
      expr <- paste(deparse(substitute(x)), rules[i], flags[i], collapse
   ="")
      test <- eval(parse(text=expr))
      x[test] <- as.numeric(Actions[i])
   }
   x
}

Yannis Tzamouranis

The question was:

Folks:
I have a question pertaining to cleaning raw data from a variety of
sources.
Instead of writing many small functions to alter data (e.g. take one
source's "999s" out and replace them with NAs, or delete certain rows), I
want to write a generic routine.

The input to this would be dataframe like this:
Flags Rules Actions
0     "<="  NA
999   "="   NA
-3    "="   removeRow
Any   my.func     0

and vectors or dataframes of raw data:
 x <- c( 235.6, 232.5, 368.2, 335.1, 209.9, 193.2,   NA, 357.8,  999,   -9,
-20, 468.1, 381.3, 393.1,   NA, 400.7)

I would like to combine the flags, rules and actions vectors so that the
first rule is combined with the first flag and then the first action is
applied if true, e.g.
"look in vector x for values that are <=0; if you find it, set it to NA"
"look in vector x for values that are =999; if you find it, set it to NA"
"look in vector x for values that are =-3; if you find it remove the row"
"apply myfunc to all elements of the vector; set those elements for which
myfunc is TRUE  to 0"

I have a couple of conceptual problems with this:
1) I want to avoid the for loops  since the input data can be LONG
2) I need to extract the elements of rules (e.g. "<=" or myFunc)  and use
as operators...
Any ideas?  Has anyone done something like this before?  If this is not the
right way to go about it, any other approaches?

Thanks,
Yannis Tzamouranis

        [WNV]  The short answer is to select just the coefficients you want.

        Here is an example based on yours (warning, untested code):

        attach(MyData)
        PolyREFI3 <- poly(REFI, 3)
        fullmod <- glm(SMM ~ PolyREFI3 + Uncle + Tom + Cobley, binomial,
MyData, trace = T)
        poly.transform(PolyREFI3, coef(fullmod)[1:4], T)
        ...

        If the polynomial coefficients are not the first four as they are
here you will need to select them more carefully, of course.  The intercept
is always the first coefficient, so that will nearly always need to be
included.

the way, but there you go...)

messages.subject: Re: ESS and plots [SUMMARY]
messages.body_plain:
I got two responses. Thanks to Andy Liaw and Henrik Nielsen for their
help. Below is my original question, their responses, and my final
solution:

ORIGINAL POST:
Sundar Dorai-Raj wrote:
> 
> I'm using splus6R2 on winpro2000 with ESS5.1.20. I would like to use ESS
> more but I've always found producing plots troublesome. Does anybody
> have any solutions they're willing to share? I don't mind dumping plots
> into a file but I would like more options than postscript, which is the
> only option I am aware of. Besides, I've only been successful with
> creating B&W postscript files (a different problem that I believe has
> been addressed by this group before).
> 

ANDY LIAW:
Are you running Splus in an iESS buffer?  If so, one alternative is to
install the Swinjava library, which gives you a java() graphics device. 
If
I remember correctly, you can't cut-and-paste from the java device to
other
apps.  The Swinjava library can be downloaded from Insightful web site.

If you want file formats other than postscript, you can use
graphsheet(type=), where type can be several things, e.g., "EMF".  (Not
sure
if graphsheet is accessible under Sqpe.exe.)

HENRIK NIELSEN:
Have ESS start S-PLUS with Java (Unix: Splus -j Windows: ?) and use
trellis.device(java.graph) when plotting.

OR 

Use encapsulated postscript which is the best graphics format around
for the kind of plots you produce with S-PLUS.  However, it is a bit
tricky to start a the graphics device i the right way:

trellis.device(postscript, color = T, file = "S.eps",
               width = 4, height = 3, pointsize = 10,
               onefile = F, print.it = F)
xyplot(NOx ~ E | C, ethanol)
dev.off()

Download http://www.imm.dtu.dk/~han/pub/graph.q to get an easier way of
starting the graphics device, e.g.:

graph(w=12, h=10, type="eps") # default color=T, w/h in cm
xyplot(NOx ~ E | C, ethanol)
dev.off()

The function may have to be modified to get it working under Windows for
type="screen" and type="spj".

MY SOLUTION:
Henrik pointed me in the right direction with trellis.device. In
WINDOWS, there are two other devices that are helpful: pdf.graph and
wmf.graph. The latter is especially important for PP slides and Word
documents. The trellis.device call would be:

# CREATE PDF PLOT
trellis.device(pdf.graph, color = T, file = "S.pdf",
               width = 4, height = 3, pointsize = 10)
xyplot(NOx ~ E | C, ethanol)
dev.off()

# CREATE WMF PLOT
trellis.device(wmf.graph, color = T, file = "S.wmf",
               width = 4, height = 3, pointsize = 10)
xyplot(NOx ~ E | C, ethanol)
dev.off()

Also note that trellis.device is not absolutely necessary. The following
works just as well:
# CREATE WMF PLOT
wmf.graph(color = T, file = "S.wmf",
          width = 4, height = 3, pointsize = 10)
plot(x=ethanol$E,y=ethanol$NOx)
dev.off()

Thanks for your help!

Sundar
--

Statistical Methods Engineer

messages.subject: Summary: Distribution with specified skewness and kurtosis
messages.subject_clean: Summary: Distribution with specified skewness and kurtosis
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to the pointers from Sundar Dorai-Raj and Joseph F. Lucke, I have
been able to use rgamma to get different skewness. Although this function
only takes positive values for skewness, it is easy to do a simple
transformation to get negative skewness. 

Not perfect but works!

Calvin King
cking at sandia.gov

My query:
I am interested in a random number generator where I can specify the
skewness and kurtosis. This will be helpful in illustrating basic
descriptive statistics to my audience. Does anyone know if such a thing
exists? Or, is there a way to build this using the available functions?

Sundar Dorai-Raj's response:
Would it be sufficient to use rgamma? The gamma distribution has nonzero
skewness and kurtosis determined by its two parameters. Any decent math
stat book (e.g. Mood, Graybill, & Boes) should have the moment
generating function from which you can evaluate higher ordinary and
central moments.

If this is not sufficient, you may have a difficult time coming up with
something easily implementable. But you can take this approach: for a
sample of size n, determine all but 4 of them. Evaluate the last 4 from
your specified mean, variance, skewness, and kurtosis. Essentially, a
non-linear system of equations.

Joseph F. Lucke's response:
You might consider the gamma distribution. With parameters a and b, it has
mean a/b, variance a/b^2, skewness coef =2/sqrt(a), and kurtosis coef = 6/a.
Here skewness coef is (3rd central moment)/sqrt(var)^3 and kurtosis coef is
[(4th central moment)/var^2]-3 to standardize for normality.
Other possibilities are the Weibull distribution and the log-normal
distribution. The moments are known, but the calculation of skewness and
kurtosis is more complicated.

messages.subject: adding and averaging likert scale or similar variables
messages.subject_clean: adding and averaging likert scale or similar variables
messages.body_plain:
All

I apologise for the slightly off topic nature of this question and will keep it 
brief (I am prepared to wear any flames and humbly apologise for the blatantly 
non S focus).

In many fields (eg psychology, marketing, political science) it is common to 
add and average ordinal ratings as though they are numbers in a way that is on 
the face of it completely inappropriate.  Similarly, people use ordinary 
correlation coefficients when they should use polychoric correlations; bog 
standard continuous response linear models when they should have some sort of 
more complex GLM; etc.  However, my hunch and to a certain degree experience is 
that at least sometimes this approach does not do too much damage to the data 
(eg more complex appropriate responses come up with similar results).

1) What are people's views?  Is it unfair, for example, to say "such scales 
should never be added and averaged"?

2) Where should I look for the literature on this? (what literature I have 
found concentrates on pointing out the flaws of common techniques and the 
importance of using some more sophisticated methods, usually one developed by 
the author; but I have not seen a comprehensive conceptual, theoretical and 
empirical comparison of the cheats' methods versus the "proper" methods)

cheers, ta, and sorry again
PE

> 
> I don't understand why the inclusion of a calling to "step.glm" (or "step")
> function gives raise to such confusion when running the function that I'd
> written. Maybe once you'd been faced with a similar problem.
> 

try this adjustment to your function:

"Poisson.Adjustment"<-function(data.phyto)
{
        (....) 
# add these two lines
assign(".data.phyto",data.phyto,where=1,immediate=T)
on.exit(rm(.data.phyto))

adjust.phyto <- glm(specie.phyto ~ . ,
family=robust(poisson,maxit=30),data=data.phyto)

adjust.phyto.step <- step.glm(adjust.phyto,scope=list(upper= ~ . ,lower=
~ upwell0days))

        (....)
}

Perhaps someone with more knowledge of Splus internals can give you a
reason. I believe it has to do with glm's use of sys.parent().
Essentially glm is looking for data.phyto in the search path and not
finding it. The above two lines assign a copy of data.phyto (named
.data.phyto) to the database. The on.exit command deletes the temporary
copy when the function is complete. Be sure to choose a name that's not
already in the database so essential data is not erased.

Regards,

messages.subject: Summary: kernel estimate with edge corrections
messages.subject_clean: Summary: kernel estimate with edge corrections
messages.body_plain:
Dear all:

 Thanks for the response from Steven Reader, Henrik Aalborg Nielsen,
Kunio Takezawa, and Yun Chiang Tai for my question on kernel
density estimate with edge corrections. Steven Reader pointed out the
splancs library by Rowlingson/Diggle, which is available at
www.maths.lancs.ac.uk/~rowlings/Splancs.

 I have been able to figure out my problem using kernel2d function in
splancs library. One thing I'd like to mention is that I'm talking to the
density estimation in two or three dimensions(e.g. space with x & y
coordinate or space-time) and edge effects due to over-/under-estimation
at the edge of the study area. 

My original question was,
We're working on creating a series of smoothing map of disease 
incidences/traffic accidents using kernel density estimation method.
We're having a serious problem related to edge effects. I am wondering
whether there's any routine/code available with edge-corrections. If
anyone know any good source of information or have similar experiences,
please let us know. 

Reply from Henrik Aalborg Nielsen,                  
 I do not have much experince in density estimation, but I would guess
that the edge effect is similar to the edge effect when using kernel
estimation for non-parametric regression; better local approximations are
needed. You might want to try Locfit by C. Loader: 
http://stat.bell-labs.com/project/locfit/
(try to have a look at Fig. 4 of the introductory paper).

>From Kunio Takezawa,
 The simplest solution to this problem is that creating histograms from
your data, and smooth them using gam() with poisson distribution.
Optimization of smoothing parameters will be carried out by CV, GCV,  or
AICc.

>From Yun Chiang Tai,
 The method I use is the local linear estimate since it could easiliy
eliminate the edge effect.I think you could find it in the Annals of
Statistics about 1990-1992.There are many articles written by Jen-Chin Fan
and Gilbel.They are the experts in this field and do provide many
theoretical proofing and good method.

 Thanks again.

Daikwon Han
SUNY at Buffalo

Thanks to Steve Weller, Sam Buttrey and Jingshan 
Zhang for their help.

 

My question was: 
 

> I am working with S-Plus 2000 for Windows. The 
machine I am using is also being used by others. I would like to create a 
personal 

> working space including a personal object 
explorer. How do I do that?

 

(1)

 

Take a look at Chapter 9 in the S-PLUS 6 User's Guide, Working 
with Objects and Databases. This describes in details how to create folders in 
the Object Explorer and what kinds of objects the S-PLUS Object Explorer 
recognizes.

 

If your machine is being used by others, the recommended way 
to maintain  a different personal workspace is to create separate S-PLUS 
shortcut icons on your desktop for each project and set the environment variable 
'S_PROJ' on the command-line of the shortcut icon, e.g:

 

C:\Splus.exe S_PROJ=C:\MySwork

 

 If you don't want to do it this way, 
you could the 'File | Chapters | Attach/Create Chapters' 
menu option to specify a chapter to attach after launching S-PLUS.

 

The way I do this is to create a new directory within Windows -- say it's 
named "c:\somewhere\Ori." Under that directory I create a "_data" directory. 
Then inside S-Plus I create an "ori" function with an attach() command in it:
 

That would look like:

 

(2)

ori 
<- function(i = 1) attach ("c:/somewhere/ori/_data", 
pos=i)

 

Then 
we you start S-Plus, type ori() and your directory will be attached in position 
1.

 

By the 
way the mechanism is slightly different in S-Plus 6; you'll need to "make a 
chapter" for your stuff the first time, before attaching.

 

 

Hope this helps.

messages.body_plain:
I'm hoping that someone here can solve a problem that none of the S-plus
wizards in my lab can solve.  I'm investigating gecko distribution at
suburban/forest edges - the data I have consists of the presence/absence
of geckos and distance from edge. Using likelihood methods, I am trying
to fit a number of different models to the distribution of the geckos,
one of which is a threshold model that takes this form:

                            p = Z if x < (or equal to) T
                            p = 0.05 if x>T

p = probability that geckos are present.
x = distance from the edge
T= threshold distance
Z = a constant value of p for distances less than the threshold distance
(T)

The value I am trying to find is the threshold distance (T) which gives
me the smallest min neg log likelihood to be compared with the min neg
log likelihood of other models (eg. GLMs).  I've tried to find a way of
doing this with the linear model function but couldn't get anything to
work.  I know that it is possible to fit a threshold model using the
'solver' function in Excel so it seems very strange that it would not be
possible in S-plus!   If anyone has any ideas on how to do this (using
s-plus 2000) I'd be very grateful if you could let me know (however I am
very much an s-plus novice, so please keep your answers as simple as
possible).

Thanks,

Lauren Keim
Department of Zoology and Entomology
University of Queensland

messages.subject: lme df and anova (summary)
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to Prof. Ripley and Renaud Lancelot for their help on this matter 
(post below).  Both pointed out that it appears that only "tube2" is a 
random factor and that it is not really nested in the fixed effect 
food.  the appropriate coding would for the random term would then be:

random= ~1|tube2

which does give sensible output, and was different and far more correct 
than what I thought was my own correction (random=~1|tube2/food)

Renaud Lancelot also provided alternative codings that account for 
different interpretations of the factors:

---

tube2 is your grouping factor (i.e. individuals over which repeated

measurements are made) and food seems to be the experimental factor of

interest. So I would do:

lme(fixed = sqrt(prot) ~ food * time + wtfsize + wtfsize:food + wtepf,
    random = ~ 1 | tube2,
    data = sueprot)

for a model with a random effect associated with the intercept (each
occurrence of tube2 has its own baseline level)

or

lme(fixed = sqrt(prot) ~ food * time + wtfsize + wtfsize:food + wtepf,
    random = ~ time | tube2,
    data = sueprot)

for a model with a random effect related to the intercept (each
occurrence of tube2 has its own baseline level) and a random effect
related to time (different growth rate for each occurrence of tube2).
This model has also a random covariance parameter between time and the
intercept, which might be removed (depending on its need given the
data):

lme(fixed = sqrt(prot) ~ food * time + wtfsize + wtfsize:food + wtepf,
    random = list(tube2 = pdDiag(form = ~ time)),
    data = sueprot)

thanks to both of you and the clarity of your help
andrew
---------

messages.subject: jackknife after bootstrap
messages.body_plain:
Dear list members,

I would appreciate some advice on the jackknife-after-bootstrap calculations
in S-Plus 6 for Windows and Efron & Tibshirani (1993), An Introduction to
the Bootstrap. In Efron & Tibshirani are the formulae and example
inconsistent or am I mistaken ?

The details:

On page 275:

var_jack(seB) = [ (n-1)/n ]  sum (from 1 to n) { ( seB(i) - seB(.) ) ** 2 }

where seB(.) = sum (from 1 to n) { seB(i) / n }

which is (I think) is implemented in S-Plus:

Professional Edition Version 6.0.3 Release 2 for Microsoft Windows : 2001 
> jack.after.bootstrap
....
func.se <- sqrt((n - 1)/n * colVars(func.vals, SumSquares = T, na.rm = T))
....

However in the example on page 277 of Efron & Tibshirani we have:

.... 'obtain the 7 values for seB(i) : 28.6, 23.3, 16.9, 17.9, 24.5, 15.4,
24.0
finally we take the sample variance of these 7 values to obtain
var_jack(seB) = 23.6'

But the sample variance has the multiplier [1/(n-1)] not the [(n-1)/n] in
the formula above, illustrated by

> x <- c(28.6, 23.3, 16.9, 17.9, 24.5, 15.4, 24.)
> n <- length(x)
> ((n - 1)/n) * sum((x - mean(x))^2)
[1] 120.1959
> (1/(n - 1)) * sum((x - mean(x))^2)
[1] 23.37143

I admit I haven't yet run the example in S-Plus starting from the raw data.

Many thanks for you time,
David.

------------------------------------

Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science.

messages.subject: Problem with Stepwise
messages.body_plain:
Dear S-Plus mailing list,

thank you very much for being so prompt in answering to my question.

Below there is a summary of the responses.

Best regards,
Helena.

On Fri, 10 May 2002, Stephen Weller wrote:

Dear Helena Nunes,

This problem is an artifact of how S-PLUS deals with objects in memory. The
'glm()' function can't 'find' data.phyto because you are calling a function
within a user-defined function.

One possible work-around:

Add the line:

assign("data.phyto", data.phyto, frame=1)

to your code, just before you call:

adust.phyto <- ....

For more information about what is going on here, look at Chapter 20 of the
S-PLUS Programmer's Guide,  'Frames Names and Values'.

Hope this helps.

Steve Weller

On Fri, 10 May 2002, Sundar Dorai-Raj wrote:

> try this adjustment to your function:
> 
> "Poisson.Adjustment"<-function(data.phyto)
> {
>         (....)
> # add these two lines
> assign(".data.phyto",data.phyto,where=1,immediate=T)
> on.exit(rm(.data.phyto))
> 
> adjust.phyto <- glm(specie.phyto ~ . ,
> family=robust(poisson,maxit=30),data=data.phyto)
> 
> adjust.phyto.step <- step.glm(adjust.phyto,scope=list(upper= ~ . ,lower=
> ~ upwell0days))
> 
>         (....)
> }

> Perhaps someone with more knowledge of Splus internals can give you a
> reason. I believe it has to do with glm's use of sys.parent().
> Essentially glm is looking for data.phyto in the search path and not
> finding it. The above two lines assign a copy of data.phyto (named
> .data.phyto) to the database. The on.exit command deletes the temporary
> copy when the function is complete. Be sure to choose a name that's not
> already in the database so essential data is not erased.

But the copy is never used!  The standard advice is to assign to frame 1
(no on.exit needed), that is

assign("data.phyto", data.phyto, frame = 1)

On Fri, 10 May 2002, Professor Brian D. Ripley wrote:

Note, there is a function stepwise(), but this is actually a scoping
problem with the use of step().

It's to do with the S scope rules, and covered in all good books on S
programming, and copiously in the S-news archives.

> Hi all,

> and calculating the cross product by
> cross.p <- (1/num.comp)*(r %*% t(r))
> and then the eigen values of the cross product
> eig.list <- eigen(cross.p)
>
> some of my eigen vector columns have opposite sign
> than the eigen vector I am getting from the MATLAB.
> But the values match identical to the values but the
> signs are opposite. Eigen values match up exact.
> I am wondering will anybody no the reason for such a
> difference. I tried using eigen(cross.p, symmetric=T)
> also. Still has the same  problem.

Look up the definition.  Eigenvectors are only defined up to a scale
factor.  If they are normalized to unit length, the sign is still
indeterminate (and a multiplier of unit modulus if the matrix is complex).
You may get different signs on different S-PLUS platforms.

However, that's not the best way to do your computation: the recommended
way is to use the svd of `r', which is a lot more stably numerically.
There is a simple relationship between the eigendecomposition of
cross.p and svd(r) which I'll leave as an exercise.

> I am using S-plus 6.0 Release 2 on Win NT.

the problem I just replace the genuine folder of my
user. The result of this process actually to delete
all documentation statement that we used. I think
everytime we run the Splus, there are some new file in

messages.subject: Summary: Question on "cut"
messages.body_plain:
Dear lists,

I submitted a question concerning "cut" yesterday.
I've received two reply.
Thank you for Shawn Boles and Prof. Ripley.
And I also received email from Insightful.

Thanks for everyone.
Mika

****** From Insightful *****
This appears to result from a lack of a method to coerce from class
"category" (the output of cut) to class "vector".  matrix() calls
array(), which attempts to do something like

        as(object, "vector")

This returns NULL when the object is of class "category".

Compare

> matrix(as.numeric(x), nrow=2)
     [,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,]    1    1    2
[2,]    1    2    2
> matrix(as.factor(x), nrow=2)
                  [,1]              [,2]              [,3]
[1,] "0.95+ thru 3.50" "0.95+ thru 3.50" "3.50+ thru 6.05"
[2,] "0.95+ thru 3.50" "3.50+ thru 6.05" "3.50+ thru 6.05"

In my opinion, the latter is the desired behavior.  A workaround to
achieve this behavior is to define a new method to do the coercion:

setMethod("as", c("category", "vector"),
        function(object, Class, coerce) as.vector(as.factor(object)))
> matrix(x, nrow=2)
                  [,1]              [,2]              [,3]
[1,] "0.95+ thru 3.50" "0.95+ thru 3.50" "3.50+ thru 6.05"
[2,] "0.95+ thru 3.50" "3.50+ thru 6.05" "3.50+ thru 6.05"

In my opinion the bug is the lack of an "as" method with signature
c("category", "vector").
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I will make sure an appropriate bug report gets filed for this issue.  Thank 
you for your help in
tracking down this problem!
************************

********From Shawn Boles *****************
Use codes()  to coerce category object to numeric vector. See below

I was able to replicate the behavior of the semicolon statement delimiter. I
was surprised by this. I don't think this would happen in unix, but can't
test at the moment.
****************************************************

************From Prof. Ripley *******************
> as(x, "vector")
NULL
> as(cut(1:6,2), "vector")
[1] 1 1 1 2 2 2

confirms that.  That's a bug.

I don't know what you actually want as a result, but
> matrix(as.factor(x), nrow=2)
                  [,1]              [,2]              [,3]
[1,] "0.95+ thru 3.50" "0.95+ thru 3.50" "3.50+ thru 6.05"
[2,] "0.95+ thru 3.50" "3.50+ thru 6.05" "3.50+ thru 6.05"
>  matrix(as.numeric(x), nrow=2)
     [,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,]    1    1    2
[2,]    1    2    2

both work.  Earlier versions (I tried S-PLUS 3.4) gave the second.
********************************************************************

> Dear lists,
>
> I have a couple of questions about "cut".
> On S-PLUS6 for Windows R4,
>
> > x <- cut(1:6, 2)
> > matrix(x,nrow=2)
>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
> [1,]   NA   NA   NA
> [2,]   NA   NA   NA
>
> If one made object inside "matrix",the result looked different.
>
> > matrix(cut(1:6,2), nrow=2)
>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
> [1,]    1    1    2
> [2,]    1    2    2
>
> On the other hand, combining two lines with ";" makes
> another result.
>
> > rm(x)
> > x <- cut(1:6, 2); matrix(x, nrow=2)
>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
> [1,]    1    1    2
> [2,]    1    2    2
>
> It looks that
> 1. there is no method to coerce category object into vector.
> 2. When one make category object inside the function,
> appropriate method exists.
>
> Regards,
> Mika

I really appreciate for all the quick answers I got from so many wonderful folks. Three questions I posted listed below and responses are followed. 

Que1: How to send a table to a designated directory?

Que2: How to add a comment line at the top of a table?

Que3: How to attach a (whole) file name in a path of directories?

Original questions:

Hello, S+ users, I have two questions regard with the write.table.

> First, is there a way to add one line of comment at the beginning of a

> table. A comment I like to put is for example, (arrive time: time1

> depart time: time 2). In here time1 and time2 are numeric and read

> from a data table and was put together using data.frame, then

> converted to a vector. Main body of a table is a matrix(3 by9).

Thank you very much for the quick and helpful answers. Now I can send a table to a certain directory with a comment at the beginning of a table, but I can not give a file name in the way I want. When I created a table using a command write.table(data,file=paste(name,".",i,sep=""),sep=","), I didn't have any trouble. Now if I use write.table(data,file="C:/directory/paste(name,".",i,sep="")",sep=","), I got error message saying name "." used illegally. I tried again after I assigned a filename_paste(name,".",i,sep=""),write.table(data, file="C:/directory/filename",sep=","), but it gave a file name literally the "filename" instead of the content of the filename. I expect something like x63314.33.1. I'll post both responses after I get answers for this question. Appreciate your help.

>From Sung:

Assuming your data frame has two columns (call it temp.mat): 

names(temp.mat)<-c("arrive time: time1", "depart time: time2") 

then, 

2. Use: 

write.table(temp.mat, "C:\\directory1\\file.txt", sep=",", dimnames.write="colnames")

You need two slashes \\, not one.

file = paste("C:/directory/", name, ".", i, sep="").

messages.subject: Re: String Split
messages.body_plain:
Dear Pierre,

I have my own simple version of strsplit (from my car library), which I 
think does what you want:

    strsplit <- function(x, split){
        if (length(x) > 1) {
            return(lapply(x, strsplit, split))
            }
        result <- character(0)
        if (nchar(x) == 0) return(result)
        posn <- regexpr(split, x)
        if (posn <= 0) return(x)
        c(result, substring(x, 1, posn - 1),
            Recall(substring(x, posn+1, nchar(x)), split))
        }

For your example:

> x <-  c("X=A=965" , "Z"  , "yd=2A",  "t=")
> strsplit(x, '=')
[[1]]:
[1] "X"   "A"   "965"

[[2]]:
[1] "Z"

[[3]]:
[1] "yd" "2A"

[[4]]:
[1] "t"

I hope that this helps,
 John

messages.subject_clean: scan(), sep, widths with a moderately large file
messages.body_plain:
People

A search of the archives failed to find a solution for this problem.

I have Windows 2000, S+ 6 release 1 (trial edition), Pentium IV 1.60Ghz, 
c.500Megs of RAM.

I have a moderately large (32MB) text file with about 260,000 rows and 10 
fields ostensibly separated by commas.  However, the file is corrupt in the 
sense that one of the fields contains commas itself.  It is thus not possible 
to treat it as a comma delimited file.  So instead I am trying to read it as a  
fixed width file.

Now, when I try, using the comma delimited option:

transhst <- scan("c:/peter/transhst",
        what=list("","","","","","","","","",""), n=40, sep=",")

It reads in the first 4 rows from the full data file fine and takes about 4 
seconds, although the resulting list is corrupt and there is a warning about 
the wrong number of fields in a line on account of the problem mentioned above.

When I try the fixed width option on a trial dataset of just the first 4 rows 
(now I have put NULLs in the "what" list as I am only interested in a few of 
the fields, which happen to be numeric) it works fine (note that there are now 
12 fields as I have made some 1 character fields consisting of a single comma):

transhst <- scan("c:/peter/test.txt",
        what=list(0,NULL,0,NULL,NULL,NULL,0,NULL,0,NULL,NULL,NULL),  
        widths=c(3,1,9,14,13,13,8,1,15,32,9,10))

Then I make room in my transhst list for the full data:

transhst[[1]] <- transhst[[3]] <- 
    transhst[[7]] <- transhst[[9]] <- numeric(260000)

But when I use the scan statement on the full file, even with a "n=48" argument 
so I only read the first 4 rows as a test, it takes apparently effectively 
forever (has been running for 70 minutes now).  The Windows task manager shows 
plenty of memory available but CPU at full usage.  What are some likely reasons 
for this?  And what can I do?  One option is reproducing the original data 
without the offending text field with superfluous commas (which I am not 
interested in particularly) so I can treat it as comma delimited but I would 
prefer to avoid this if possible.

cheers and TIA
PE

messages.subject: More GUI problems
messages.body_plain:
In using S-Plus 6 (release 2) on my IBM laptop running Windows 2000, I have 
been finding that when I make a graph ("traditional" graphics) and try to 
copy it on the clipboard, I often get the following errors:

"Copy graph sheet page" results in an S-Plus warning, something like 
"Invalid operand. May be missing values."  Any subsequent attempt to use 
the clipboard results in an S-Plus crash.

Needless to say, that is a nasty consequence when using S-Plus in 
time-critical situations. In my field, any analyses done on a laptop are 
usually under strict time deadlines and a great deal of pressure. It's not 
pleasant to find that S-Plus lets me down when I need it most. It also 
doesn't help my colleagues believe my claims that S-Plus is a better tool 
than Excel for quantitative work.

Why can't Insightful use software quality tools to find and fix, once and 
for all, these erratic problems with its interface?  I use many other 
programs, and while some are just as bad, there are others (the Adobe 
applications come to mind) that rarely, if ever, crash.  Certainly, no 
other program I use regularly is as unreliable as S-Plus, on any of the 
three computers I use regularly.

Can anyone offer suggestions for avoiding this type of problem?  Is R any 
less crash-prone?

MHP
(From the road.)

Disclaimer: Opinions expressed are personal ones, and not claimed to be 
those of my employer.

> "Copy graph sheet page" results in an S-Plus warning, something like 
> "Invalid operand. May be missing values."  Any subsequent 
> attempt to use the clipboard results in an S-Plus crash.

This problem is caused by a bug in your printer driver resetting the
floating-point control word.  There's more information on the known bugs
page on our site at:

http://www.insightful.com/support/faqdetail.asp?FAQID=131&IsArchive=0

The tech support team can provide a patch which works around this
problem; the easiest solution is to contact them to get it.  (We don't
simply make it available for download as it takes a bit of human
diagnosis to determine the correct fix.)

> Why can't Insightful use software quality tools to find and 
> fix, once and 
> for all, these erratic problems with its interface?  I use many other 
> programs, and while some are just as bad, there are others (the Adobe 
> applications come to mind) that rarely, if ever, crash.

messages.subject: Re: Question re objects() and remove()
messages.body_plain:
Dear Peter,

At 10:42 AM 5/16/2002 -0400, you wrote:
> Unlike many, I like to keep just one workspace (perhaps this is only
> because I am new to S-Plus).
>
>
>
> I thought a way to keep things a little organized would be to use object
> names that have one or more periods (.) for objects I don't want to
> delete; and then remove those without a period
>
>
>
> But I can't figure out a way to do this.
>
>
>
> Any help appreciated

You can use grep to filter the names. The exact form depends upon the 
version of S-PLUS. For example, the following expression works in S-PLUS 
2000 for Windows:

        objects()[grep('*.*', objects())]

while the following works in S-PLUS 6.0 for Windows:

        objects()[grep('\\.', objects())]

Once you have the names, you can use remove to erase them -- e.g., 
remove(objects()[grep('\\.', objects())])

Note, however, that you'll also be removing some variables generated by 
S-PLUS with names including periods, such as .Last.value.

I hope that this helps,
 John

messages.subject: missing
messages.body_plain:
In response to my question [at end of this message] on multiple
imputation, I received two replies.  I thank Jim Schimert and Tim
Hesterberg for their very helpful comments.  For those interested, I
copied Tim Hesterberg's reply below.

#-------- Tim Hesterberg wrote -------------------------

#Generate list of starting values using a bootstrap
start <- list()
for(i in 1:5)
  start[[i]] <- paramIter(emGauss(cholesterol,
                          subset=sample(1:28,14,T), prior="ml")) # draw
5 imputations from 5 parallel chains, each run for 50 iterations
cholesterol.imp <- impGauss(cholesterol, prior="non",
                            start=start, control=list(niter=50))

Second, help(impGauss.methods) gives specifications for the `start'
argument, including this text:
          For several chains, start may be a list of such lists, a class
          "Gauss" object, or a list of "Gauss" objects.
          For a list of lists, each interior list must contain the two
          components mu and sigma. The number of imputations equals the
          length of the outermost list.
          A class "Gauss" object is the paramIter component of a class
          "missmodel" object, produced by routines such as mdGauss,
          daGauss, and emGauss. This is a matrix with as many rows as
          there are imputations.

Third, this code:
for(i in 1:5)
        start[i,] <- paramIter(emGauss(twin.d0, subset = sample(x =
                1:nrow(twin.d0), size = 0.5*nrow(twin.d0), replace = T),
        prior = 'ml'))[1,]
tries to shoehorn paramIter objects into columns of an ordinary matrix;
some information is lost.

Tim Hesterberg

#--------my question----------------------

I am trying to run multiple imputations through DA using the missing
        data library [Splus 6R2, Win2K].  I was trying to write a start
function
        but I am having trouble understanding how many columns need to
be in the
        start matrix [code below].  In other words, what is the relation
between
        columns in the start matrix and the number of variables
subsequently
        used in the impGauss command?

Respectfully, 
Frank R. Lawrence

messages.subject: Help to speed up a for loop (leave-one-out procedure),
messages.subject_clean: Help to speed up a for loop (leave-one-out procedure),
messages.body_plain:
Dear S-Plus users,

I am trying to implement a "leave-one-out" procedure for the predictions of a 
model and I managed to do that... but in a very uneffectively way (details 
below). To be specific: I would like to (1) parameterize a model with every 
observation except one (the model was specified previously), (2) make the 
corresponding prediction for this one observation left out, (3) repeat until I 
have a vector of predictions for every observation. There is a further 
complexity: I have a large amount of previously specified models (about 70), so 
I would want to repeat the steps above for each one of these models. I have 
windows 2000, 256 Mb RAM and my clumsy code is:

> version

S-PLUS 2000 Professional Edition Release 2 for Microsoft Windows : 1999 

First I set a vector with the number of previously specified models: 

lista <- c("aegcau.escala150.b2", "siteur.escala150.b2", "trotro.escala150.b2")

Then, a for inside a while loop:

comienzo <- proc.time()

predicciones2 <- 1:nrow(tmpESCALA150)         # tmpESCALA150 has the response 
(n=1144) and predictors

predicciones <- numeric(nrow(tmpESCALA150))          # set up an empty vector 
for predictions

n <- 1

while (n < length(lista)+1) {                    # to visit every element of 
"lista" 

for (i in 1:nrow(tmpESCALA150)) {     # to visit every element of original 
database (tmpESCALA150)

predicciones[i] <- 

predict.gam(

gam(eval(parse(text=(paste(as.character(lista[n]), "$formula")))), 

data=tmpESCALA150[-i,], family=binomial),         # model$formula is previously 
specified

tmpESCALA150[i,], type="response")                 # predict response for the i 
observation left out

}

predicciones2 <- cbind(predicciones2, predicciones) 

                # clumsy, but I finally need a data set with the predictions 
("predicciones2")

n <- n+1

}

predicciones2

tiempo <- proc.time()-comienzo

tiempo/60 

The loop takes 254 min to complete with only three specified models (in 
"lista"). A loop for a single model takes 45  min. I am afraid that looping 
through 70 models would be unaffordably slow. 

Any suggestions to speed up the loop would be appreciated,

Javier Seoane
Department of Applied Biology
Estación Biológica de Doñana, CSIC
Avda. María Luisa s/n
41013, Sevilla
SPAIN

Olivier

messages.subject: passing GUI data to variables
messages.body_plain:
Greetings;

I have had an enormous amount of help from the Insightful tech support team,
esp. Truc-Giang Pham with GUI questions.  The GUI functions are complex but
very powerful, anyone with some spare time could probably write an entire
(and probably successful) book on just the GUI functions in S+.

I'm trying to get some different perspectives on this problem:

Truc kindly created a two-page GUI that is created like this: (using the
TESTGui function)

guiCreate("FunctionInfo",Function="TESTGui",PropertyList = c("TESTProp0",
"TESTPage1", "TESTPage2")) 

and displayed like this:

guiDisplayDialog("Function", Name= "TESTGui")

and I want to pass names selected by the user from two wide MS List Boxes, 1
radio box, and 1 String box into 4 separate variables.  I have a function
that's called from guiCreate above:

TESTGui <- function(...){ 
        MS.List.Box#1.data_rbind(...)
        MS.List.Box#1.data<<-MS.List.Box#1.data
        #MS.List.Box#2.data_rbind(...)
        #MS.List.Box#2.data<<-MS.List.Box#2.data
        #Radio.Box.data_rbind(...)
        #Radio.Box.data<<-Radio.Box.data
        #String.Box.data_rbind(...)
        #String.Box.data<<-String.Box.data
}

The question is:  how do I pass my variable names (not objects but the
actual names from the dialog boxes) to 4 different vectors.  There will be
an unknown number of objects selected from the boxes (can I use nargs(...)
or do I need to use rbind(...)?) and I need to put them into 4 vectors. 

1) Do I need to use 4 separate functions, 1 for each list box or can I use
one function for all 4 dialogs?  I'm guessing 4 separate functions.
2) The function seems to be trying to eval(...) my selections instead of
passing the names from the dialog boxes.  How do I grab only the names?

Thanks for any help, I've had a lot of help from a lot of people and I'd
like to thank everyone with suggestions.

Sincerely,

Phillip Stafford
Motorola Life Sciences

messages.subject: survival, ties, and frailty advice II
messages.subject_clean: survival, ties, and frailty advice II
messages.body_plain:
Dear listers-
SPLUS2000R3 + R1.5 WINNT4

This is not yet a summary to my previous post about predicting with a 
frailty term (to which Geir Egil Eide has commented) and I preface this 
with the caveat that the question is related to survReg/coxph and frailty, 
but is not really a mechanics question.  Read on if you'd like.

I've asked a variant of this before, but here goes again.

Imagine a data set with 6 hospitals and 50 patients monitored in each 
hospital.  Each hospital was randomly assigned to a 2 treatment x 3 diet 
factorial design such that each of the 100 patients were receiving the same 
treatment and diet combination in the hosipital and clearly there is one 
hospital for each treat*diet combination. Moreover, there is the chance 
(lets assume) for a significant number of ties.

Would an apporpriate/acceptable model be
survReg(Surv(time,cens)~treat*diet+frailty(hospital)?
or
coxph(Surv(time,cens)~treat*diet+frailty(hospital),method="efron")

In reality, I have a data set with 168 hospital equivalents and from 
50-2500 patients/hospital.  There are 2x3x2x2x2x4=192 treatment 
combinations each with a unique number of patients... the treatments, in 
full factorial, thus exceed the number of "hospitals", meaning that some of 
the cells in the model are empty (some hospitals, and all of the patients 
in that hospital, have been lost during the study). Moreover, there are 
alot of ties within each "hospital".

Philisophically, hospital should be a random or frailty term... but as the 
number of treatment combinations = or exceeds the number of "hospitals", is 
it still appropriate? And the ties....

Any advice would be appreciated (including give up ;)
cheers
andrew

messages.subject: Summary: passing dialog data to variables
messages.subject_clean: Summary: passing dialog data to variables
messages.body_plain:
To S+ Group:

My original problem was to take text items from 4 different dialog boxes, 
either all 4 at once or one by one, and pass those names to a data.frame().  
The consensus is to use the callback function.  Using cbGetCurrValue() and 
cbGetOptionList() grabs data from the dialog boxes.  Be careful about including 
quotes and/or commas in the list returned from the dialog box with useQuotes=T. 
 Also, I was unaware of the ..n feature using formal input (...), this gives 
you access to the nth arg in the input.  

This code is the usage of cbGetActiveProp() from the dialog example 
'dlgcomm.ssc'.  That and Widgets.ssc are two very handy examples.  If Widgets 
would take input and assign the inputs to variables it would be a perfect 
dialog example showing an abundance of dialog features.

cbParentDlg <-function(df)
{if( ! IsInitDialogMessage(df) && (cbGetActiveProp(df) == "parentButton") )
        { guiModify( "Property", Name= "childParentId", 
          DialogControl= "Invisible", DefaultValue=cbGetDialogId(df) );
          guiDisplayDialog("Function", "childDlg", T);
        }               
        dfParentTemp <<- df
        df}

Thanks again to Stephen Weller, Jean-Paul Fox and David Lorenz, but especially 
to Truc-Giang because this also works perfectly:

TESTGui_function(arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4){ 
        from.wide.MS.list<<-unlist(arg1)
        from.wide.MS.list2<<-arg2
        from.string.box<<-unlist(arg3)
        from.radio.buttons<<-arg4
        invisible(from.radio.buttons)
}
        

############################################################################
You will need to use what is called a dialog 'callback function' to update
and retrieve information from an active dialog. Take a look at the
'dlgcomm.ssc' Splus sample script in your '<SHOME>\samples\dialogs'
directory. Also check out the discussion in Chapter 17 of the
S-PLUS Programmer's Guide: Extending the Graphical User Interface.

Yes, you will need to use a separate callback function for each dialog. You
can grab the names selected in each dialog using the functions
'cbGetCurrValue()' and 'cbGetOptionList()'. Take a look at the 'dlgcomm.ssc'
example.

Stephen Weller
###########################################################

 

>guiCreate("FunctionInfo",Function="TESTGui",PropertyList = 
> c("TESTProp0",
> "TESTPage1", "TESTPage2")) 

This creates a dialog with two pages, but variables within these pages are
not defined. So define:
guiCreate("Property", Name = .... ) you can define the variables, names if
it is a string or a checkbox, see chapter 17 Pragrammer's Guide.

With the following command
guiCreate("Property", Name="TESTPage1", Type="Page",
PropertyList="variable names" ....)
one can point variables to TESTPage1 of the dialog.

The input variables must also be defined within the 
guiCreate("Functioninfo", ......,.....,....
Argumentlist="#0=input1,
              #1=input2,
                #2=input3,
                #3=input4,
                #4=input5")

Then, the input of the dialog is defined and one can define a function,
TESTGui to perform some operation with this input.  
Jean-Paul Fox.

Phillip,
   The output from MS List Boxes is a comma separated string, if UseQuotes
is T in the property definition.  You can use unlist(unpaste(output, sep
=",") to create a vector from one of the input boxes.
  I also think that you should name your input into TESTgui.  It is not
easy to deal with dots.  Each unmatched argument (in ...) can be referred
to in the form ..n, where n is an integer identifying the sequential
argument in ... .  So ..1 refers to the first argument in ... .
Dave

David Lorenz

messages.subject: Re: Problems loading the sm library
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to Dennis Murphy, who sent me this website, maintained by Brian
Ripley:
http://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/MASS3/Winlibs/
The website contains a version of the sm library that works with R4 and
SPLUS 6.x

The problem was that the libraries were created for R3 and SPLUS 3.x and
are not compatible with later releases.
SPLUS' Steve Weller pointed out that I could try the migration wizzard but
as Sherry Lamonica (SPLUS again) points out, that facility is a simple
translation that cannot deal with complex issues such as multiple
inheritance.  The latter have to be dealt with manually, naturally.

My original question follows:

messages.subject_clean: Summary: Proportional hazards model with interval censored data
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to all who responded to my question and suggested S-PLUS functions and literatures. To summarize the practical aspects, censorReg() works with interval censored data (however, plot.censorReg() did not work in my case because I did not have any exact deaths). The online help of coxph() may seem encouraging, however coxph() handles only interval truncation, not interval censoring.

Chuanpu

At 10:44 AM 5/7/02 -0400, you wrote:

>interval censored data? Additionally, if one has a proposed model under this

>scenario, are there any S-PLUS functions that can show the goodness of fit

>diagnostics (e.g., Cox-Snell residuals)?

   In Cooperation with Japanese Society for Artificial Intelligence

              IEEE ICDM 2002: Call for Tutorials
              **********************************

The 2002 IEEE International Conference  on Data Mining (ICDM '02) will
include tutorials  providing in-depth background  on specific subjects
in data mining.  The recency of the data mining field, and the variety
of disciplines  that are represented,  lead to many  possibilities for
good tutorials:

   * End-to-end  descriptions  of the  practical  application of  data
     mining technology (i.e., applications that may be "typical" for a
     paper, but  provide an example of  issues faced in  a data mining
     project that would generalize to problems faced by the conference
     attendees)  in  emerging  data mining  application areas  such as
     bioinformatics,  medical applications,  electronic commerce,  Web
     Intelligence and Business Intelligence.
   * Surveys   of  new   and   developing  research   areas  in   data
     mining (e.g.,  areas  of  structured, textual, temporal, spatial,
     multimedia,  Web, distributed, scientific  data mining, data pre-
     processing,  data reduction,  data sampling,  feature  selection,
     feature  transformation,  man-machine interaction  in data mining
     and visual data mining).
   * Short  courses  on  areas  of  machine  learning,  databases,  or
     statistics  that  may  be   "old  hat"  to  specialists  in  that
     discipline,  but  are  new   to  a  majority  of  the  conference
     attendees. (e.g., an introduction to Hidden Markov Models).
   * An in-depth coverage of a past research breakthrough  that is now
     becoming a mature technology.

The topics of interest  fall within those described  in the conference
Call for Papers (Home Page: http://kis.maebashi-it.ac.jp/icdm02
                 Mirror Page: http://www.wi-lab.com/icdm02).

Submission Details
==================

The tutorial proposal should include the following:

  1. Title and abstract of the tutorial;
  2. Intended audience. Include prerequisite knowledge required of the
     attendees, and  the expected areas  of interest (e.g., a tutorial  
     on statistics for people applying data mining  tools vs. a tutorial  
     on statistics  for people  building  data mining tools);
  3. Length of time needed (e.g., half day or full day); and
  4. Short biographies of the presenters.

Tutorial materials such  as handouts and slides should  be included if
available,  but are  not required  for submission.  However, providing
such materials will show depth  and maturity of the tutorial, and will
be a strong factor in the selection process.

Please   send  a   soft   copy   (preferred)  of   your  proposal   to
washio at ar.sanken.osaka-u.ac.jp, or a hard copy to:

     Prof. Takashi Washio (Tutorials Chair)
     I.S.I.R., Osaka University
     8-1, Mihogaoka, Ibaraki City,
     Osaka, 567-0047,
     JAPAN

Notice 
=======
(1) Honorarium of $500 is provided to the speaker per a half-day 
    tutorial. (If multiple speakers give a half-day tutorial, it is
    shared by the speakers.)
(2) Travel expenses of $500 (speaker is from outside of Japan) and
     $100 (speaker is from inside of Japan) are provided to the tutorial 
     speaker.  (If multiple speakers give a tutorial, it is shared 
     by the speakers.)

Important Dates
===============

     June 30, 2002: Tutorial submissions.
     July 31, 2002: Acceptance notices.
   August 31, 2002: Camera-ready copy of tutorial handouts.
  December 9, 2002: ICDM '02 tutorials.

messages.subject: Re: geometric mean
messages.body_plain:
<I know that this question is not new but I haven't seen the answer yet.>
the correct answer probably is 'that depends...'

<Is it correct to work with the log-data and then make the antilog of the
confidence interval limits?.>
in general, under log and-or exponential transforms, variances do not
transform correctly, but percentiles do.

under different assumptions about how the errors arise you can derive
different types of asymptotic confidence intervals.

typical approaches for finding c.i.s for geometric means are 

1) using some distributional assumption such as the data has a log-normal
distribution.
logging the data (as you said), finding a normal c.i. for the mean of the
logged data, and 
1a)transforming the percentiles. in general, this gives no estimate of
standard error but you may not need it.  also, if you are transforming the
empirical distribution to get the percentiles, 
you will be limited in the alpha you can use (or have to form a random
c.i.).
1b) making assumptions that allows you to transform the variance, such as
the data has a log-normal distribution.  

note: if you assume that your data, X, is log-normal(mean=mu, standard
deviation-sigma), then sigma, the standard deviation of ln(X), provides a
measure of dispersion of X/exp(mu) in the sense that
[exp(-1.96*sigma),exp(1.96*sigma)] is a 95% c.i. for X/exp(mu).  so under
the assumption of log-normal X, the anti-log of the standard normal c.i.
provides a c.i. for X.
(actually, this note is probably all you wanted)

2) using a taylor linearization.
if X is your random variable, and GM(X) is the geometric mean of X, then:
GM(X) approximately= E(X) - var(X)/[2E(X)]

your english seems fine, but i would recommend that you talk to a spanish
speaking statistician at your university.

do you have a theory as to how your errors arise?
do you need an estimate of variance or only the confidence interval?
can you treat you data as an i.i.d. sample?
do you think your data is log-normal?
do you think a taylor approximation is a really fun way to get an estimate?

a few things you might need to think about.

i'm sure i got a few things wrong in here but the list is good at correcting
me and, as i said, you should really ask someone about this.

good luck with your problem.
bob
